video.title: The End Of Monthly AI Subscriptions?

summary: George McConnell explains Higgsfield's new pay-per-use API, which replaces subscriptions (up to 270 USD/month annual) with per-image/per-second video pricing he says is cheaper than fal. He shows the web playground, copying an 'agent prompt' into Claude Code or Codex, creating API keys tied to billing, and spend analytics (3.93 USD for a 15-second video). There is no business idea beyond cost control for content creators producing for clients. Takeaway: usage-based media APIs driven by agents lower and clarify the cost of AI content production.

tactics.name: Drive Higgsfield from a coding agent
steps: Sign up for the Higgsfield API
Pick a model and copy its 'agent prompt' from the quick start
Paste into Claude Code or ChatGPT Codex and answer its setup questions
Create an API key tied to billing and give it to the agent
Monitor spend in the analytics dashboard (daily burn per model)

quote.speaker: George McConnell

tactics.name: Track per-asset cost when producing for clients
steps: Use the API analytics to see spend per video/model
Use those numbers to price work for other people

quote.text: so that if you're creating things for other people, you can easily build them
quote.speaker: George McConnell

lessons.lesson: Pay-per-use APIs beat subscriptions when usage is uneven, and let you compute exact cost per deliverable.
Plug media-generation APIs into your existing agent rather than using each tool's web UI.

quote.text: now with the API, you no longer have to do that. You could do it all through your agent
quote.speaker: George McConnell

lessons.lesson: Compare per-second model prices across providers (Higgsfield vs fal) before committing.
Keep API keys tied to a billing balance and track daily burn.

evidence_quality.rationale: Promotional tool walkthrough with vendor pricing; no business results.
